h: How to Look Like You Know What You're Doing
p: Okay, you probably won't fool anyone on your first go, but a few simple pointers will have you looking a lot steadier. Keep your knees bent, lean very slightly forward and resist the urge to stand bolt upright. Push off with one foot at an angle, glide, then do the same with the other. Little and often wins the day.

Stopping is where most beginners come unstuck. The easiest method is to point your toes slightly inwards and gently push your heels out, a bit like a snowplough on skis. Practise it near the side before you build up any speed, and you'll feel a lot more in control.

If you're bringing kids, gloves are non-negotiable, and a helmet is a sensible shout for younger children if you've got one. Waterproof trousers aren't a bad idea either for little ones who spend more time sitting on the ice than skating on it.

Medway has a lot to offer beyond the rink. Riverside Country Park in Gillingham runs along the Medway estuary and is great for a breezy walk with lots of birdlife. Rochester is just along the road, with its Norman castle, its cathedral and a high street full of character that Charles Dickens knew well. Chatham's Great Lines Heritage Park offers big views over the river. Put a skate together with any of those and you've got a varied day out in Kent.
